approachQuestion.prompt:
Dial adjustment

A circular dial has L equally spaced ticks, labeled 0 through L-1 clockwise. It currently reads a and should read b; input readings may include any whole number of revolutions, so labels are interpreted modulo L. Return a signed number of ticks of minimum absolute value: positive clockwise, negative counterclockwise. If both directions are equally short, return the nonnegative one.

Example 1: L=12,a=11,b=1 -> 2.
Example 2: L=12,a=1,b=11 -> -2.
Example 3: L=12,a=0,b=6 -> 6.
Example 4: L=10,a=-1,b=1 -> 2.

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= L <= 10^9; -10^18 <= a,b <= 10^18. Return one integer. In the implementation language, remainder may be negative for negative operands. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Compute the clockwise residue d=((b-a) rem L+L) rem L. Return d when d<=floor(L/2), else d-L.
options.feedback: The normalized value lies in [0,L-1]. Comparing it with half the period selects the shorter direction and keeps a nonnegative exact half-turn.

options.text: Normalize a and b separately into [0,L-1]. Let d=bNormalized-aNormalized; if d>floor(L/2) subtract L, and if d< -floor(L/2) add L. For even L replace d=-L/2 by +L/2.
options.feedback: Separate normalization yields the same cyclic displacement. The wrap corrections give minimum magnitude, with the explicit negative half-turn correction enforcing the tie rule.
For L=12,a=11,b=1 it returns -10 instead of 2; equivalent revolutions must be removed.

options.text: Take d=(b-a) rem L and return d unless d>L/2, in which case return d-L; do not correct negative d.
options.feedback: With negative-remainder semantics, L=12,a=11,b=1 gives -10 instead of 2. Negative residues need normalization.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (normalized-displacement). Let L be the number of ticks, using fixed-width arithmetic and unit-cost remainder. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(log L) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Fixed modular normalization replaces looping around the dial.
